clue.text: Possibly con artist's relocated in setting of Alcatraz

indicators.note: something relocated has been moved about, so the painter's letters are rearranged
the reworked name sits inside the word meaning possibly

blocks.note: 'say' introduces a possible example, as in 'say, ten'
the painter Francis Bacon, an artist whose surname ends in 'con'

explanation.surface: A swindler is shipped off to the famous island prison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Con artist' reads as a swindler, and Alcatraz did hold cons, but here it is the painter Francis Bacon, whose surname ends in CON. His letters are rearranged inside SAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Alcatraz is the former prison island lying in San Francisco Bay, California.

clue.text: I would be separately involved in stake

definitions.text: I would be separately involved in stake

indicators.note: the two short words go into the word for stake at two different points rather than together

blocks.note: to set money on something is to stake it
contraction of 'I would'
taken as written

explanation.surface: A gambler says they would like a separate stake in the action.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Separately' means the two short pieces go in at different points, not side by side. Read whole, the clue also describes the answer: a wager I would make apart from the main stake.
explanation.definitionFit: A side bet is an extra wager placed alongside the main one, so it is a separate involvement in the stakes.

clue.text: Putative Oscar winner? No egg on Emma's face

indicators.note: a face is the front of something, so only the opening letter of the name is kept

blocks.note: taken as written
'egg' is old military slang for a bomb or mine
the first letter of Emma

explanation.surface: An actress hoping for an Oscar is spared an embarrassing moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Egg on face' suggests embarrassment, but egg is slang for an explosive. The question mark marks the definition as an example: someone shortlisted is only a possible winner.
explanation.definitionFit: A nominee for an award is a candidate who might win it, so a supposed or potential winner.

clue.text: Show on radio means to pay toy company fine

indicators.note: on the radio we only hear words, so what counts is their sound rather than their spelling

blocks.note: readies is slang for cash, the means to pay, and a teddy is a toy bear
standard abbreviation for company
OK means fine, all right

explanation.surface: A radio advertiser explains how to settle up with a toy firm.
explanation.walkthrough: Readies is British slang for ready money. Ready Steady Cook was a long-running BBC TV cookery contest.
explanation.definitionFit: Ready Steady Cook is a television programme, so it is a show in the broadcasting sense.

clue.text: Your favourite compiler, short and sweet

indicators.note: something short has been cut, so the last letter of the phrase is dropped

blocks.note: No. 1 setter, with the 1 written as I: the setter cheekily calls himself your top crossword setter

explanation.surface: The setter praises himself as brief and charming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short and sweet' looks like one idiom, but it splits: short is the cut, sweet is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A noisette is a hazelnut chocolate, a kind of confectionery, so a sweet in the British sense.

clue.text: Light on board meeting items to be raised

indicators.note: what is on board is carried within, so the letters sit inside the clue's words
in a down clue raising letters means reading them from the bottom up

blocks.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: Board members are told some matters will come up at the meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On board meeting' looks like a boardroom agenda; the board is just a container for the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To light a fire or fuse is to set it alight, which is what ignite means.

clue.text: Detective's associate on the spot puts "Sn" in upper-case symbols

indicators.note: the words for on the spot, puts and the tin symbol go inside the case symbols

blocks.note: a cap is a covering worn on the head, the upper part of the body
tags are labels or symbols
in means present, at the scene
has in the sense of places, as in 'has it on the shelf'
Sn is the chemical symbol for tin

explanation.surface: Someone on the scene inserts a chemical symbol into capital letters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upper-case symbols' reads as capital letters, but it splits into headwear (worn on the upper body) and labels.
explanation.definitionFit: Captain Hastings is Hercule Poirot's friend and sidekick in Agatha Christie's novels.

clue.text: Unnamed abductor of treasures smuggled into poor country

indicators.note: without a name means losing N, the standard abbreviation for name
smuggled goods are hidden inside something else

blocks.note: Lord Elgin removed the Parthenon sculptures, the Elgin Marbles, to Britain
bum as an adjective means of poor quality

explanation.surface: A nameless art thief sneaks his loot into a struggling nation.
explanation.walkthrough: Elgin drops the N for 'name' and goes inside BUM.
explanation.definitionFit: Belgium is a country in western Europe.

clue.text: My solver's time done!

blocks.note: the setter speaking: his solver is you, so the solver's is your
an eon is a vast stretch of time

explanation.surface: The setter tells the solver that their time is up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Done!' is the exclamation accepting a bet or challenge, not 'finished'.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying 'you're on' accepts a wager, as does the exclamation 'Done!'.

clue.text: For a very long time this will punish mother country

definitions.text: For a very long time this will punish

blocks.note: a dam is an animal's mother
synonym

explanation.surface: A motherland that will punish its people for ages.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition comes first and is long: the whole opening describes eternal punishment.
explanation.definitionFit: Damnation is condemnation to hell, a punishment lasting for eternity.

clue.text: Turn up carrying The Greatest Indian Food

indicators.note: turning the whole construction round means reading it backwards
the short word carries the boxer's name within it

blocks.note: taken as written
Muhammad Ali called himself The Greatest

explanation.surface: Someone appears bringing the finest Indian dish.
explanation.walkthrough: The capitals on The Greatest point to Muhammad Ali's nickname.
explanation.definitionFit: Pilau is spiced rice cooked in stock, a staple dish of Indian cuisine.

clue.text: Exchange elements that will get you by

blocks.clueFragment: elements that will get you by
blocks.note: the chemical elements B (boron) and Y (yttrium) spell out 'by'

explanation.surface: Swapping just enough basics to get by.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get you by' sounds like scraping through; it means the elements whose symbols make the word BY.
explanation.definitionFit: To bandy words is to exchange them, tossing them back and forth.

clue.text: Converted Italian both subject and object of writer's drawn-out period

blocks.note: a former trattoria, an ex-trat, once converted to another use; trat is short for trattoria, an Italian restaurant

blocks.clueFragment: both subject and object of writer's
blocks.note: the writer refers to himself as I as subject and ME as object

explanation.surface: A writer describes a long period in which an Italian is both subject and object.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Converted Italian' suggests a religious convert; it is a restaurant that has become something else.
explanation.definitionFit: Extra time is the additional period played when a match is drawn, a drawn-out stretch of play.

clue.text: Players in football match bouncing with a score before the hour mark

definitions.text: a score before the hour mark

indicators.note: bouncing someone throws them out, as a doorman does

blocks.note: two teams of eleven take the field
W is the abbreviation for with

explanation.surface: Footballers on the field are bouncing with a score before the hour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Score' looks like goals, but it is twenty minutes on the clock.
explanation.definitionFit: Twenty to the hour is a time twenty minutes, a score of minutes, before it strikes.

clue.text: Not quite saying in advance one will give you the time of day?

definitions.text: one will give you the time of day?

indicators.note: not quite all of the word, so its final letter is left off

blocks.note: a gnome is a pithy maxim
on means ahead, as in 'send it on'

explanation.surface: Someone almost says hello ahead of time, offering the time of day.
explanation.walkthrough: Gnome in the sense of an aphorism is the root of gnomic. The question mark warns that 'give you the time of day' is literal here.
explanation.definitionFit: A gnomon is the pointer on a sundial whose shadow shows the hour.

clue.text: A nightmare having to carry unhinged brief case?

blocks.note: nuts means mad
hell is a nightmare experience

explanation.surface: A bad dream of lugging a broken-hinged briefcase.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer the lower word carries the upper one on top of it. 'Brief case' plays on briefcase: a shell is a case, and 'in a nutshell' means briefly.
explanation.definitionFit: A nutshell is the hard casing of a nut, and the word also stands for a very brief summary.

clue.text: Caught Mike's predecessor by the end

blocks.note: C is the cricket scoring abbreviation for caught
in the NATO alphabet Lima comes just before Mike
X is the multiplication sign, read as 'by' in measurements like 2 x 4

explanation.surface: A man named Mike's forerunner is caught at last.
explanation.walkthrough: Mike is the NATO code word for M, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: A climax is the culminating point of a story or event, its high point towards the finish.

clue.text: Not completely parched after putting down party aperitif

indicators.note: not the complete word, so its last letter is dropped

blocks.note: a camp is a faction or party
arid means dried out

explanation.surface: A thirsty guest reaches for a drink after setting down the party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party' suggests a celebration, but it is a political camp.
explanation.definitionFit: Campari is a bitter Italian liqueur drunk before meals, a classic aperitif.

clue.text: Sort of stand nailing the onset of sexual knowledge

indicators.note: nailing something pins it firmly inside
the onset of a word is its beginning, so only its first letter goes in

blocks.note: a one-night stand, with one written as I
first letter of sexual

explanation.surface: A one-night stand brings carnal knowledge.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is about sex; 'sort of stand' gives 1-NIGHT, the I being the numeral one.
explanation.definitionFit: Insight is perceptive understanding, a deep form of knowledge.

clue.text: On retirement day at university opening notes impress

indicators.note: retiring means withdrawing backwards, so the short pieces run in reverse
the reversed group goes in and opens up the word for money

blocks.note: standard abbreviation
taken as written
standard abbreviation
banknotes are cash

explanation.surface: A retiree's university leaving-day speech notes are meant to impress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opening' looks like the start of a speech; it means the notes are opened to take the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut a dash is to make a stylish, striking impression on people.

clue.text: A very successful manager heading off rival after defeat?

indicators.note: the head of a down word is its top letter, here taken off

blocks.note: taken as written
standard abbreviation
Arsène Wenger, long-serving and successful manager of Arsenal football club

explanation.surface: A winning football manager sees off a rival after a loss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heading off rival' looks like defeating a competitor; heading off cuts the manager's first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An avenger seeks to repay a wrong, as an opponent might after a loss; the question mark flags the loose fit.

clue.text: Hospital let me think it's OK to elevate bone

indicators.note: in a down clue elevating letters means writing them from the bottom up

blocks.note: standard abbreviation, as on road signs
the sound of hesitation while thinking
sure means yes, all right

explanation.surface: A hospital patient wonders whether it is safe to raise a broken limb.
explanation.walkthrough: The medical surface makes 'elevate' look like raising an injured arm.
explanation.definitionFit: The humerus is the long bone of the upper arm.

clue.text: Accommodation for sleeping bears you've picked up?

indicators.note: picking something up by ear means hearing it, so sound matters, not spelling

blocks.note: to bear young is to give birth, so bears means births as a verb

explanation.surface: Where do hibernating bears sleep?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bears' looks like the animals hunting for a den; it is the verb, to give birth.
explanation.definitionFit: Berths are bunks or sleeping places on a ship or train.

clue.text: Withdrawing gross deception, seeing chippy's softer side?

indicators.note: something withdrawing goes back the way it came, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: a gross is a total sum
hype is misleading promotion
seeing as means because, like as

explanation.surface: A carpenter drops his rough pretence and shows a gentler nature.
explanation.walkthrough: A chippy is British slang both for a carpenter and for a fish-and-chip shop; it is the shop here.
explanation.definitionFit: Mushy peas are mashed marrowfat peas served as a soft side dish at British fish-and-chip shops.

clue.text: In service of which one's a jolly hot bath!

blocks.clueFragment: In service of which one's a jolly
blocks.note: a jolly is slang for a Royal Marine

explanation.surface: A bather exclaims how splendidly hot the water is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jolly hot bath' reads as an exclamation, but a jolly is a member of the Royal Marines (RM).
explanation.definitionFit: A therm is a unit of heat energy, used for gas bills, so loosely the heat in a hot bath.

clue.text: Group's leader runs through past problems

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter alone
passing through something means being inside it

blocks.note: ago means in the past
first letter of Group
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A band's frontman goes back over old troubles.
explanation.walkthrough: Aggro is British slang for trouble or aggravation.
explanation.definitionFit: Aggro means hassle and aggravation, so trouble or problems.

clue.text: Brief word about foal, precocious youngster?

indicators.note: a brief version is cut short, so the word loses its final letter
about means going round, so the shortened word surrounds the young horse

blocks.note: a term is a word
a foal is a wee nag, a small horse

explanation.surface: A quick remark about a young horse that is ahead of its years.
explanation.walkthrough: TERM loses its M and wraps WEE NAG; wee is Scottish for small and a nag is a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A tweenager is a child of about ten to twelve acting older than its age, hence precocious.

clue.text: "To each his own" – slogan for Bassett's lorry?

blocks.note: first meaning: a saying that people differ in their tastes
second meaning: Bassett's make Liquorice Allsorts, so their lorry carries all the sorts

explanation.walkthrough: Bassett's is the British confectioner famous for Liquorice Allsorts, a mixed bag of liquorice sweets.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says the world contains every kind of person, much as 'to each his own' tolerates differences.
